files.path: SUPPLEMENTARY web/viewer.html (1354 lines, over the 800 limit)

rule_objections: Rule is narrow but defensible. In an app like pdf.js the ids are the only handles the JavaScript uses (getElementById), so id-as-variable is useful; custom elements and data-l10n-id attributes (the real localisable names) are not indexed, by rule.

Every id becomes a symbol named just by its value, so viewer.html gives 308 symbols (the element identity is lost: no tag, no parent); ids like `viewer`, `toolbar`, `sidebar` collide with identifiers in other languages in a mixed repo.
findings: Against the stated rule: 375 expected, 375 found (right names, lines, kind variable); 0 missed, 0 spurious. My expected list came from a regex scan that blanks comments, <script> and <style>, drops empty/space/template ids, and matched the table exactly for all four files. No ids from comments or scripts leaked.
Symbols per file equal the id count (12 / 13 / 42 / 308): no flood beyond the ids themselves.
The three largest html files under 800 lines in pdf.js are small (185/141/137), so I added the 1354-line viewer.html as a supplementary 4th file and counted it in totals.
Text search works (`search Sidebar` returns the html files).
not_done: Not exercised: server-side template syntax in attributes, duplicate ids, ids in tags with syntax errors.
